behavior.arguments: rdi = struct pointer; fields read: table lo at [rdi], table hi at [rdi+0x8], limit at [rdi+0x18]; rsi = search key. No other input register is read; r8, rcx, rax, and rdx are all written inside the window before use.

edges.above_limit: keys [10, 20, 30], limit 30, search 31 -> count - 1 = 2 via the early shortcut, without searching.
edges.at_limit: keys [10, 20, 30], limit 30, search 30 -> count - 1 = 2 via the early shortcut; the shortcut fires on key >= limit, not only key > limit.
edges.empty_span: no entries, limit 5, search 3 -> 0 on the search path.
edges.empty_span_at_limit: no entries, limit 0, search 0 -> count - 1 wraps to 0xffffffffffffffff via the early shortcut; the empty-span 0 applies only on the search path (key < limit).
edges.past_end: keys [10, 20, 30], limit 100, search 50 -> 3, one past the last entry.
edges.single_entry_past: keys [7], limit 10, search 8 -> 1, one past the entry.
edges.unsigned_compare: keys [2^63], limit 2^64 - 1, search 1 -> entry 0 under the unsigned compare (a signed compare would have taken the less-than path and returned 1).

behavior.entry_shape: Opens with endbr64; six conditional branches plus one unconditional jmp join; three rets (shortcut, loop exit, empty span); two intra-body nop paddings (5-byte nopl, 10-byte nopw, 6-byte nopw); no calls inside.
behavior.loop_rule: count = (hi - lo) arithmetic-shift-right 3 (span in bytes, sar floors toward -inf for a negative span, but a non-positive span exits before the loop). While looping: mid = count arithmetic-shift-right 1; entry = lo + mid*8; key_entry = [entry] (single dereference); if key_entry >= rsi unsigned: if mid == 0 return the entry's index, else count = mid and repeat; else lo = entry + 8, count = count - mid - 1, and repeat only if count > 0, else return the lo index.
behavior.return_rule: If key >= limit (unsigned): count - 1, without searching. Else if the span is non-positive: 0. Else the lower-bound index: the first entry whose key is >= rsi (unsigned), or the insertion point (one past the last probed entry) when every probed key is < rsi, assuming a well-formed span (a multiple of 8) and ascending keys. For a positive span that is not a multiple of 8, count truncates (span sar 3) and the loop still walks the truncated count. For a negative span on the search path the window returns 0 without reading any entry; on the shortcut path it returns the (negative) count - 1.

coordinate_system: ELF virtual addresses, without a guessed loader or Ghidra rebase. The ELF section table maps .text with file offset = VA - 0x1000; the retained .eh_frame has equal file offset and VA. The tools resolve sections rather than assuming one global VA/file-offset relationship.

incoming_pattern_scan.note: Byte-pattern scan over the full .text section (70,370,352 bytes) for e8 sites whose rel32 lands on the window start; one site found in one caller FDE, confirmed as an instruction start by linear disassembly from the caller FDE start. This is explicitly not a complete xref census: indirect calls, tail jumps, and PLT references are out of scope for the scan.
incoming_pattern_scan.relocation_note: No relocation record of any type in any .rela.* section names this window as addend (full-section scan: 80,022 .rela.dyn + 278 .rela.plt entries).

scout_corrections: The round-16 scout note listed this window (backup B4, the last real backup after ranked #1-#4 and backups B1-B2, with B3 rejected as a twin) with FDE [0x52ca970, 0x52ca9e3), 115 bytes, 13 padding bytes, one direct caller (boundary-confirmed), no naming relocation, and nearest claimed window dual-zero test 0x5341920 (packet #36) 0x76fb0 away. Every scouted element verified exactly, with two refinements to the scout's rule summary, stated head-on: (1) the count - 1 shortcut fires when key >= limit, not only when the key is above the limit (the jb branch is taken on key < limit, so key == limit takes the shortcut); (2) the empty-span 0 applies only on the search path (key < limit) — an empty span with key >= limit returns count - 1 wrapped to all-ones. No numeric correction to the scout's FDE, padding, caller, or relocation numbers was needed.
